significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that "transmission strength scales with the overlap between teacher and student empirical NTK / gradient subspaces," together with the form-(ii) claim that permutation alignment partially restores transmission; this fixes expected transmission across graded-overlap configurations rather than merely identifying a trait direction. It would establish both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanistic account of the shared-initialization dependence reported in Cloud et al.'s 2025 Subliminal Learning paper, replacing an undifferentiated shared-weights requirement with a measurable geometric determinant and a sufficiency intervention. Failure of both predictions would informatively rule out tangent-space overlap and basis mismatch as the main explanation, although failure of re-basin alone would not exclude other shared-initialization mechanisms; despite unspecified effect thresholds, "scales with" versus no systematic relationship and restoration versus none are distinguishable states. In the topic-substitution check, merely asking how subliminal learning works would not merit this score: the specific overlap law and basis-alignment consequence are materially more constraining than the median extension hypothesis on this topic.

reach.justification: The claim supplies two named handles: "empirical NTK / gradient subspace" overlap as a predictor and "aligning a student to a teacher via permutation symmetry (git re-basin)" as an intervention. Both can operate ex ante—overlap can forecast whether transmission will occur and alignment is applied "before finetuning"—giving researchers or distillation auditors an action window rather than only explaining an observed failure. After per-model re-extraction, the proposed relation still predicts that greater overlap yields stronger transmission, but its asserted practical scope is mainly independently initialized, architecture-compatible models and "related model lineages," with uncertain transfer to different architectures or large transformers; Ainsworth et al.'s Git Re-Basin work also makes permutation alignment a concrete but architecture-constrained handle. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: subliminal learning alone offers no transferable screen or pre-finetuning intervention, whereas these claim-specific handles could affect how related models are distilled, audited, or gated.
